emerging_technology: Large language models (generative AI for text)
intended_application: Ambient clinical documentation: drafting visit notes from recorded doctor-patient conversations for physician review
organization: National medical scribe and transcription services company (~1,500 human scribes and transcriptionists)
industry_sector: Healthcare business services; HIPAA business associate
business_need: Clients are trialling ambient AI documentation tools that could replace contracted human scribes; management must decide how the company's service offering responds
users_stakeholders: Hospital and clinic clients, physicians, scribe workforce, sales team, investors, compliance
capabilities_constraints: Strong client relationships and workflow knowledge; large trained workforce; limited software engineering and no ML team; margins depend on scribe labour utilisation
risk_consequence_context: High business consequence: core revenue is billed per scribe-hour or per note; documentation errors carry clinical and contractual liability
management_question: Should the company build, partner for, or resell ambient AI documentation, and how should its human-scribe service be repositioned?
time_horizon: Strategy decision in 6 months; impact over 1-3 years
additional_context: Business model: revenue from direct online sales of its own apparel brand; competitive advantage is brand, design, and speed to market. Copywriting is an internal cost, not a product the company sells.
